text: Imagine you are running happily on the playground, playing catch with your best friends. Suddenly, a fast bicycle zooms past you, almost bumping into you! You freeze in your tracks. Why didn't the bicycle stop? What could have happened if you didn't freeze?

Have you ever wondered why your parents always hold your hand while crossing the road? Or why teachers ask you not to run in the corridors? What would our daily life look like if everyone did whatever they wanted without looking out for others?

content.title: The Invisible Safety Shield
content.description: Just like a brave knight wears strong armor to protect himself in a story, we have an invisible shield in real life! Every time you look both ways before crossing the road, or keep away from fire, your shield gets stronger and keeps you protected.

text: This invisible shield is powered by **Safety Rules**. Safety rules are simple habits and instructions we follow to keep ourselves and the people around us safe from harm, whether we are at home, at school, or on the road.

content.definition: The state of being protected from danger, harm, or injury.
Black and white stripes painted on the road where people can safely walk across.

text:
Here are some of the most important rules to power up your shield:

**1. At Home:** Never play with sharp objects like knives or scissors. Do not touch electrical switches with wet hands.
**2. On the Road:** Always walk on the footpath. Cross the road only at the zebra crossing when the pedestrian light is green.
**3. At School:** Do not run up and down the stairs. Wait for your turn on the swings.

content.text: Many children think that running across the road quickly is the safest way. That is a BIG mistake! Cars are much faster than we think. Always stop, look left, right, and left again before crossing safely.

content.question: What is the main reason we have safety rules?
options: To protect ourselves and others from getting hurt
To win a prize at school

content.question: Which of these is a safe thing to do at home?
options: Putting your fingers inside electrical sockets
Playing with matchsticks in the kitchen
Putting your toys away after you finish playing

text: Think about a time when you saw someone doing something unsafe, like playing with a sharp pencil. Explain in your own words to your parents why that was dangerous. Teach them the correct safety rule!

content.text: Safety rules connect with everything we do! When we learn about 'Our Body', keeping safe means not injuring our bones. When we learn about 'Transport', safety means following traffic signals. The knowledge of safety is a superpower that helps you everywhere.

content.title: Safety Detective Project
content.text: It is time to be a Safety Detective! Walk around your house with an adult. Try to find three things that could be unsafe (like a toy left on the stairs, or water spilled on the floor). Create a 'Safety Fix' for each danger and write it down!
